entries.name: AppStoreFoundation
entries.note: n/a: the foundation of the Mac App Store, an Apple store service. BifrOSt's store is its own catalogue (springboard/src/shell/store/mod.rs), so there is no Apple store to mirror.

entries.name: AppStoreKit
entries.note: Product pages with get, progress and open states, and an updates tab, work on BifrOSt's own catalogue. There is no embeddable product view for other apps, and reviews and in-app purchase are not mirrored.

entries.name: AppStoreUI
entries.note: Gap: the app rating and review sheet with star rating, nickname and written review. Build it in the store sheet layer once the catalogue API has review endpoints; springboard/docs/apps.md lists none today.

entries.name: AppStoreUtilities
entries.note: Only the Info.plist is in the reference index; the component's role is not confirmed.

entries.name: AppSubscriptions
entries.note: Subscription billing and renewal for the vendor's store accounts; BifrOSt has no billing service for store accounts.

entries.name: AppSupport
entries.note: Resource-only bundle of city and country name tables (CityInfo.db and localized tables); the reference index shows only data files, so its runtime role is not confirmed.

entries.name: AppSupportUI
entries.note: Only the Info.plist is in the reference index; the component's role is not confirmed.

entries.name: AppSystemSettings
entries.note: The settings model behind the Settings pages: preference keys such as the appearance and accent keys, and their values. It does not mirror the reference's pane registry or its extension points.
entries.ready_note: Settings model (shell/settings.rs) with its preference keys and tests; the pane registry is not mirrored.

entries.name: AppSystemSettingsUI
entries.note: Settings pages for display, sound, network, accounts and storage, with search over every pane. The reference's payment, messaging and secure element panes are not mirrored.
entries.ready_note: Settings panes and search over them (shell/settings.rs, shell/settings_search.rs) are tested; payment, messaging and secure element panes are not mirrored.

entries.name: AppUserEvents
entries.note: Only the Info.plist and version file are in the reference index; the component's role is not confirmed.

entries.name: AppearancePreferencesFramework
entries.note: Light, dark and automatic appearance with an accent colour, published to native apps through the appearance portal. The reference's glass tint amount and appearance-button settings are not mirrored.
entries.ready_note: Appearance model with light, dark and automatic modes, accent colour and the cross-fade (render/src/appearance.rs) is tested; the appearance portal publishes it to apps.

entries.name: Apple80211
entries.note: Wi-Fi scan, join, saved networks and power save work through the supplicant and the network service. Apps get no SDK query API for interfaces or networks, and access point mode is not mirrored.
entries.ready_note: Wi-Fi scan, join, saved networks and power save through the supplicant (net/wifi.rs, net/wpa.rs, shell/wifi_page.rs), tested.

entries.name: AppleAccount
entries.note: Sign-in, recovery and legacy contacts for the vendor's own cloud identity; BifrOSt accounts come from its own service, with a local account in springboard/src/shell/account.rs.

entries.name: AppleAccountTransparency
entries.note: Account transparency daemon (appleaccounttransparencyd) for the vendor's cloud account; BifrOSt has no vendor account service.

entries.name: AppleAccountUI
entries.note: Sign-in, recovery-contact and account-update sheets for the vendor's cloud identity; they belong to the same identity service as the account framework above, which is n/a.

entries.name: AppleAppSupport
entries.note: Only the Info.plist and version file are in the reference index; the component's role is not confirmed.

entries.name: AppleCVA
entries.note: Gap: face landmark, face fitting and vehicle detection models ship with the framework and BifrOSt has no detection layer. Build face or object detection only if the photo or camera apps need it, on a pure-Rust model runner.

entries.name: AppleCameraExclaveSISPTestServices
entries.note: Test services for the camera image signal processor that runs in the hardware exclave of the reference's own silicon; they serve that vendor's camera hardware test rig and have no counterpart in BifrOSt's camera code.

entries.name: AppleCameraISPExclaveKitServices
entries.note: Camera image signal processor services that run in the hardware exclave of the reference's own silicon; BifrOSt enumerates ordinary camera devices (springboard/src/shell/camera/devices.rs), so the component has no counterpart.

entries.name: AppleConvergedFirmwareUpdater
entries.note: Firmware update delivery for the vendor's own hardware; BifrOSt has no counterpart for Apple firmware.

entries.name: AppleCredentialManager
entries.note: Credential sync for the vendor's cloud identity; BifrOSt keeps credentials in its own keychain (springboard/src/keychain.rs).

entries.name: AppleDepth
entries.note: Depth data from the vendor's front camera hardware; BifrOSt captures through generic V4L2 cameras.

entries.name: AppleDepthCore
entries.note: Depth processing core for the vendor's camera hardware; BifrOSt has no depth sensor support.

entries.name: AppleDeviceQuerySupport
entries.note: private framework, no plausible owner found

entries.name: AppleDisplayTCONControl

entries.name: AppleFSCompression
entries.note: Compression for the vendor's APFS file system; BifrOSt runs on btrfs and ext4, which have their own compression.

entries.name: AppleFirmwareUpdate

entries.name: AppleFlatBuffers
entries.note: private framework, no plausible owner found

entries.name: AppleGPIOUser

entries.name: AppleGVA

entries.name: AppleGVACore

entries.name: AppleHIDTransportSupport

entries.name: AppleIDAuthSupport

entries.name: AppleIDSSOAuthentication

entries.name: AppleIDSetup

entries.name: AppleIDSetupDaemon
entries.note: Daemon for the vendor's Apple ID setup; BifrOSt has no counterpart.

entries.name: AppleIDSetupUI
entries.note: Apple ID setup interface for the vendor's account service; BifrOSt has no counterpart.

entries.name: AppleISPEmulator
entries.note: Image signal processor emulation for the vendor's camera hardware; BifrOSt captures through V4L2 with no ISP emulation.

entries.name: AppleIntelligenceReporting
entries.note: Feedback reporting for the vendor's on-device intelligence service; BifrOSt has no such service.

entries.name: AppleIntelligenceReportingProcessing
entries.note: Feedback processing for the vendor's on-device intelligence service; BifrOSt has no such service.

entries.note: private framework, no plausible owner found

entries.name: AppleKeyStore

entries.name: AppleLDAP

entries.name: AppleLOM

entries.note: Media store interface of the vendor; BifrOSt has the PC App Store and the media player, with no purchase service.

entries.name: AppleMobileFileIntegrity

entries.name: AppleNVMe

entries.name: ApplePDPHelper
entries.note: Reference image 26A434 holds only the framework directory skeleton (no binary, no Info.plist, no payload entries) and no other index entry names it, so its purpose cannot be determined here.

entries.name: ApplePhotonDetectorServices
entries.note: Reference image 26A434 holds only the framework directory skeleton and no other index entry names it, so its purpose (likely an optical sensor service) cannot be confirmed here.

entries.name: ApplePushService
entries.note: Client for the vendor's push servers that deliver messages to Apple ID services (device push tokens for iCloud and App Store); BifrOSt has no push server and delivers its notifications locally (springboard/src/shell/usernotif.rs). Only the framework directory skeleton is in the reference image, so the classification rests on the name.

entries.name: AppleSRP
entries.note: Secure Remote Password exchange used to sign in to Apple ID account servers; BifrOSt has no Apple ID sign-in, and its account sign-in is a separate service (bifrost-cloud). Classified from the name only, since the reference image holds just the framework directory skeleton.

entries.name: AppleSauce
entries.note: Reference image 26A434 holds only the framework directory skeleton (no binary, no Info.plist) and no other index entry names it, so its purpose cannot be determined here.

entries.name: AppleScript
entries.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/control.rs (JSON-RPC app control socket); springboard/sdk/src/intents.rs (App Intents); springboard/core/src/script/ (scripting language); springboard/cmd/src/osascript.rs
entries.note: Apps can be driven by control-socket calls, intents and AppEvents. A small AppleScript-style language runs in osascript: tell blocks, handlers, variables, try, do shell script and dictionary commands. Not covered: the Script Editor app, the sdef dictionary format (dictionaries live in manifest.toml instead), recording, and the reference object model in full.
entries.ready_note: Control socket, intents and the osascript command language are built and tested.

entries.name: AppleServiceToolkit
entries.note: Reference image 26A434 holds only the framework directory skeleton and no index entry names it, so its purpose cannot be determined here.

entries.name: AppleSplatRendering
entries.note: The name suggests a point-splat (Gaussian splat) renderer, but the reference image holds only the framework directory skeleton, so the purpose is unconfirmed and the row stays os.

entries.name: AppleSystemInfo
entries.note: The system information app reads hardware, software, firewall and host statistics from the machine. Not covered: the reference's per-category hardware profile and any SDK API for apps to query the same data.
entries.ready_note: Hardware, software and host statistics probes are built and tested; the per-category hardware profile is not mirrored.

entries.name: AppleThunderboltRDMADetection
entries.note: n/a: Apple-only Thunderbolt RDMA link detection between Macs (name-based; the reference binary is not in the extract). Apple hardware with no PC counterpart.

entries.name: AppleTracingSupportSymbolication
entries.note: gdb resolves addresses to symbols and reads core dumps, which covers crash symbolication. Not covered: symbolicating trace and signpost files as the reference tracing tools do.
entries.ready_note: gdb is installed and resolves addresses and reads core dumps, which is the crash symbolication path.

entries.name: AppleVA
entries.note: Hardware video decode runs in the media module, which covers the accelerated playback path. Not covered: the reference video accelerator driver bundle (System/Library/Extensions/AppleVADriver.bundle), which is specific to Apple graphics hardware.

entries.name: AppleVPA
entries.note: Reference image 26A434 holds only the framework directory skeleton and no index entry names it, so its purpose cannot be determined here.

entries.name: AppleVirtualPlatform
entries.note: Hosts the platform identity services (com.apple.AppleVirtualPlatform.Identity.Virtio.vzplugin and AppleVirtualPlatformIdentityService.xpc in the reference index) that give virtual machines of the reference system their identities; these depend on Apple's hardware and boot chain, so they have no meaning on an Arch host.

entries.name: AppletTranslationFramework
entries.note: No on-device text translation exists in BifrOSt. Build a local translation engine behind an SDK translation API, with Icelandic and English as the first language pairs.

entries.name: ApplicationFirewall
entries.note: Nothing sets an inbound policy per application: the sysinfo app only reads the nftables and iptables state. Build an application-level firewall: a settings page that writes nftables rules for each app's listening ports, applied by a service at boot.

entries.name: ArchetypeUI
entries.note: Reference image 26A434 holds only localisation resources for this framework and its directory skeleton, with no binary, so its purpose cannot be determined here.

entries.name: ArgumentParserInternal
entries.note: Internal copy of the Swift argument-parser library that the reference system's Swift command-line tools link; BifrOSt's command-line tools are Rust and parse their own arguments. Classified from the name only, since the reference image holds just the framework directory skeleton.

entries.name: AskPermission
entries.note: Shows the reference system's permission-request sheet (AskPermissionUI.app in the reference index) for parental approval through the vendor's family account service; BifrOSt has no family account service, so the sheet has no counterpart.

entries.name: AskTo
entries.note: Part of the reference system's family request feature (Ask to Buy and similar parental approval requests), which runs on the vendor's family account service; BifrOSt has no family accounts. Classified from the name only, since the reference image holds just the framework directory skeleton.

entries.name: AskToCore
entries.note: Core model of the reference system's family request feature (parental approval requests), which depends on the vendor's family account service that BifrOSt does not have. Classified from the name only, since the reference image holds just the framework directory skeleton.

entries.name: AskToDaemon
entries.note: Background daemon for the reference system's family request feature (parental approval requests), which relies on the vendor's family account service that BifrOSt does not have. Classified from the name only, since the reference image holds just the framework directory skeleton.

entries.name: AskToMacBridge
entries.note: Bridges the reference system's family request views into its desktop (AskToMacViewService.xpc in the reference index), a path that exists only for the vendor's family accounts; BifrOSt has no family accounts or such a bridge.

entries.name: AskToPeopleBridge
entries.note: Connects the reference system's family request feature to its contacts (the people of a family account), listed under System/iOSSupport in the reference index; BifrOSt has no family accounts, so there is no contact-side counterpart to connect to.

entries.name: AskToUI
entries.note: User interface of the reference system's family request feature (parental approval prompts), which depends on the vendor's family account service that BifrOSt does not have. Classified from the name only, since the reference image holds just the framework directory skeleton.

entries.name: AssertionServices
entries.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/sleep.rs (logind sleep and idle inhibitors through systemd-inhibit)
entries.note: Sleep and idle assertions are held and listed through systemd-inhibit, and the shell reads the blockers before sleeping. Not covered: display-sleep and user-activity assertions, which the shell does not hold yet.
entries.ready_note: Sleep blockers are read through systemd-inhibit and refused in bare::sleep, with unit tests.

entries.name: AssetCacheServices
entries.note: Content caching for the reference system's own software updates and service downloads, served through a locator XPC service (AssetCacheLocatorService.xpc in the reference index); it depends on the vendor's content servers. BifrOSt's own update daemon (springboard/updated) fetches from BifrOSt's servers and has no peer caching, so the cache has no counterpart.

entries.name: AssetCacheServicesExtensions
entries.note: Manager and tetherator XPC services (AssetCacheManagerService.xpc, AssetCacheTetheratorService.xpc in the reference index) extend content caching for the reference system's own update and service downloads, which come from the vendor's servers; BifrOSt has no such download source.

entries.name: AssetMetricsCoreV2
entries.note: Collects usage metrics for the reference system's media and store assets to report to the vendor's analytics services; BifrOSt sends no telemetry to a vendor service, so it has no counterpart.

entries.name: AssetViewer
entries.note: Previews of files in apps and the shell's preview panel are covered by the peek module. Not covered: the reference preview and thumbnail extensions (RAQLPreviewExtension, RAQLThumbnailExtension) that render asset packages.
entries.ready_note: Preview model for files in apps and the shell peek panel (sdk/src/peek.rs) is tested.

entries.name: AssistantActionSuggestion
entries.note: private framework, owner Intents; from SDK matrix siri-kit.json
entries.ready_note: Apps declare [[intent]] tables in manifest.toml and serve them on their control socket. Search and the Shortcuts action library list and run an installed app's shortcut intents (shell::intents::runnable_shortcuts). The assistant answers with intent cards that run only after the user confirms them, and reads answers aloud when Speak Answers is on. Voice recognition is not built: nothing turns speech into an intent request, so Siri's spoken requests are not covered.

entries.name: AssistiveControlSupport
entries.note: The reference ships switch-control templates (ascconfig bundles) for scanning-based input. BifrOSt has a pure switch-scan model (springboard/ui/src/switch_scan.rs: scan order, auto and manual steps) that nothing calls, and no switch input or switch-layout template format. Wire the model into the accessibility layer (springboard/src/shell/atspi) with a template format.

entries.name: AsyncAlgorithmsInternal
entries.note: Internal copy of the Swift async-algorithms library used by the reference system's Swift runtime; BifrOSt is written in Rust and uses its own async primitives, so it has no counterpart. Classified from the name only, since the reference image holds just the framework directory skeleton.

entries.name: AtomicsInternal
entries.note: Internal copy of the Swift atomics library used by the reference system's Swift runtime; BifrOSt is written in Rust and uses the standard library atomics, so it has no counterpart. Classified from the name only, since the reference image holds just the framework directory skeleton.

entries.name: AttentionAwareness
entries.note: Attention-detection framework, known by name only: the reference index extract holds no binary or strings for it, so its exact job is unconfirmed and it stays os.

entries.name: AttributeGraph
entries.note: The graph that tracks which values a view reads and re-evaluates on change is modelled as automatic dependency tracking over observable values. Gap: there is no attribute graph that updates view bodies incrementally.

entries.name: AudioAccessoryAssetManagement
entries.note: Downloads and stores firmware and assets for the vendor's wireless earbuds and other audio accessories, which BifrOSt does not ship or pair with.

entries.name: AudioAccessoryServices
entries.note: Pairing and settings protocol for the vendor's audio accessories; generic Bluetooth audio devices are not this vendor-specific service.

entries.name: AudioAnalytics
entries.note: Audio quality and usage analytics that report to the vendor's analytics service; BifrOSt's audio server keeps no telemetry.

entries.name: AudioAnalyticsBase
entries.note: Shared event model of the vendor's audio analytics service, which uploads usage events to the vendor; BifrOSt has no such upload path.

entries.name: AudioAnalyticsExternal
entries.note: External-facing part of the vendor's audio analytics service, which reports to the vendor; BifrOSt has no such reporting.

entries.name: AudioDSPAnalysis
entries.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/fourier.rs (FFT and DFT); springboard/audio/engine/src/graph.rs (tap nodes, TapRing)
entries.note: Spectral analysis exists as an FFT and DFT model and as tap nodes that copy audio out of the graph. Gap: no system analysis service publishes DSP measurements to other clients.

entries.name: AudioDSPGraph
entries.note: The node graph with format-checked connections, a cycle check and offline rendering is built. Gap: there is no system-wide DSP graph that assigns processing to devices.

entries.name: AudioDSPManager
entries.note: Hosting and registration of audio processing units exists. Gap: no manager decides which DSP stages run for each device or session.

entries.name: AudioPasscode
entries.note: Audio passcode service (name only). Its purpose could not be confirmed from the reference index extract, so it stays os until the framework can be inspected.

entries.name: AudioPasscodeDSP
entries.note: DSP half of the audio passcode service (name only). Purpose could not be confirmed from the reference index extract; stays os.

entries.name: AudioServerApplication
entries.bifrost: springboard/audio/hal/src/lib.rs (client library over the control socket)
entries.note: Clients get, set and listen to the audio object model and run IO procedures on real-time threads. Gap: the server does not yet track per-application identity beyond per-app volume in the policy crate.

entries.name: AudioServerDriver
entries.note: The driver interface between the audio server and its device drivers exists, with null and loopback drivers. Gap: virtual devices are described as data only and no user-space plug-in is loaded to publish them.

entries.name: AudioServerDriverTransports_Base
entries.note: The shared-memory transport between the audio server and its clients is built and layout-tested. Gap: there is no pluggable base transport for drivers other than this one.

entries.name: AudioServerDriverTransports_IOA2
entries.bifrost: springboard/audio/alsa/src/lib.rs (ALSA driver over the kernel uapi)
entries.note: Device transport goes through ALSA over the kernel uapi. Gap: there is no IOAudio-family user-client transport, which is not needed on this OS.

entries.name: AudioServerDriverTransports_IOP
entries.note: Device IO is a trait that drivers implement. Gap: no separate provider-based transport exists; device IO is served by the ALSA driver only.

entries.name: AudioSession
entries.note: Audio session categories, activation, interruption and route-change notifications are modelled in the SDK. Gap: the sound server does not yet enforce session categories across applications.

entries.name: AudioSessionServer
entries.note: The session manager's decisions (defaults per role, ducking, permissions, per-app volume) are pure state machines. Gap: the daemon's control loop is not yet wired to the HAL client.

entries.name: AudioToolboxCore
entries.note: private framework, owner AudioToolbox; from SDK matrix audio-toolbox.json

entries.name: AudioTranscriptionAnalysis
entries.note: Speech-to-text over a pluggable recognition backend and analyzer input sources exist. Gap: there is no system transcription analyzer service shared by applications.

entries.name: AudioTransportCommon
entries.note: The control-socket protocol between clients and the audio server is defined and shared. Gap: transport code common to drivers is not factored out beyond the shared-memory ABI.
entries.ready_note: Control-socket protocol shared by clients and the audio server (audio/types/src/control.rs), tested.

entries.name: AuthKit
entries.note: Account authentication for the vendor's iCloud and store services. BifrOSt accounts are its own cloud service, so this framework has no BifrOSt counterpart.

entries.name: AuthKitUI
entries.note: Sign-in and two-factor interface for the vendor's account services, which BifrOSt does not use.

entries.name: AutoBugCaptureCore
entries.note: Automatic capture of diagnostic reports that are uploaded to the vendor's feedback service; BifrOSt uploads no diagnostics.

entries.name: AutoFillCore
entries.note: Field content types and the saved-login fill model exist, and the browser fills sign-in forms from them. Gap: there is no system-wide autofill extension point for other applications.

entries.name: AutoFillUI
entries.note: One-time-code detection and credential identities for suggestions exist as pure models. Gap: no system suggestion panel draws them yet.

entries.name: AutoLoop
entries.note: Name only; the reference index extract holds no binary or strings for this framework, so its purpose could not be confirmed and it stays os.

entries.name: AutoUnlock
entries.note: Unlocks the Mac from a paired Apple Watch over the vendor's proximity protocol, which needs the vendor's watch hardware.

entries.name: AutoUnlockDaemon
entries.note: Daemon for watch-based unlock, which needs the vendor's watch hardware and pairing service.

entries.name: AutomationMode
entries.note: Developer automation-mode permission for UI test tools (the matching daemon row is also os). BifrOSt has app control sockets but no permission gate for automation; the purpose is confirmed by name only.

entries.name: AvailabilityKit
entries.note: Feature availability checks (name only). The purpose could not be confirmed from the reference index extract, so it stays os.

entries.name: AvatarKit
entries.note: Rendering of animated avatars for the vendor's messaging and video features, which BifrOSt does not ship.

entries.name: AvatarKitContent
entries.note: Avatar art and content for the animated avatar feature, which BifrOSt does not ship.

entries.name: AvatarPersistence
entries.note: Storage of the user's avatar records for the animated avatar feature, which BifrOSt does not ship.

entries.name: BNNSCoreAIDelegate
entries.note: Typed inference functions and multidimensional arrays are built. Gap: there is no delegate that hands graphs to a vendor accelerator; inference runs on BifrOSt's own kit.

entries.name: BNNSGraphPCC

entries.name: BNNSOdieDelegate

entries.name: BackBoardServices

entries.name: Backup
entries.note: Snapshot retention is modelled (timemachine.rs: hourly, daily, then weekly tiers over btrfs snapshots) and the shell's own data is archived with checksums (backup.rs). Not covered: a scheduler for system volumes and restore from snapshots.
entries.ready_note: Retention tiers over btrfs snapshots (shell/timemachine.rs) and checksummed archives (shell/backup.rs) are tested.

entries.name: BagKit

entries.name: BarcodeSupport

entries.ready_note: EAN-13 and Code 39 decoding in ui/src/barcode.rs is tested.

entries.name: BatteryCenterUI

entries.name: BatteryUIKit

entries.name: CVAMatrix

entries.name: CVNLP
entries.note: Ships word language models for European languages and segmentation models for Chinese, Japanese and Korean, which predictive text and word splitting need; build predictive text on the text input path, starting from springboard/sdk/src/spellcheck.rs.

entries.name: CacheDelete
entries.note: Recently Deleted is emptied of items older than 30 days (trash::purge). core::cache_purge plans an LRU purge of per-app caches while skipping running apps, but the shell does not execute the plan or trigger it under disk pressure. Built 2026-10-17: core::cache_purge::execute removes the planned folders under the cache root and never reaches outside it (tests execute_tests). Still open: nothing calls the plan under disk pressure yet.
entries.ready_note: The purge plan is executed: the low-space trim removes the planned apps' Library/Caches folders (least recently used first, running apps kept, links not followed), via core cache_purge::execute and shell storage purge_app_caches. Tested by the execute tests and the storage test. The trigger is the existing low-space guard (is_low), not a separate disk-pressure policy.

entries.name: CacheExpert
entries.note: Investigated: the reference files index has no resource, launch item or plist for this framework, so the name (a cache manager, by the name alone) is not confirmed.

entries.name: CalDAV

entries.ready_note: CalDAV and CardDAV client and sync (sdk/src/dav_client.rs, dav_sync.rs) are unit tested; lab verification is still pending.

entries.ready_note: Event store write side (save, remove, commit, reset) in ui/src/calendar_store.rs is tested.

entries.name: CalendarDraw
entries.note: The calendar grid for the Day, Week and Year views is drawn in timeview.rs; the reference invitation artwork is not mirrored.

entries.ready_note: Calendar event and recurrence model used by the calendar app (ui/src/calendar*.rs) is tested.

entries.ready_note: Calendar connected to the shell's alarms and Up Next feed (connect.rs), tested.

entries.ready_note: Calendar intents (show a date, show an event, create an event) in intents.rs, tested.

entries.name: CalendarNotification

entries.ready_note: Event alarms computed in alerts.rs and scheduled as notifications through connect.rs, tested.

entries.name: CalendarUI

entries.name: CalendarUIKit
entries.note: The calendar views the desktop app shares (timeview.rs); BifrOSt has no separate toolkit layer for them, and the tablet build of these views is not verified.

entries.name: CalendarUIKitInternal

entries.name: CallIntelligenceRuntime

entries.name: CallsPersistence

entries.name: CallsUtilities
entries.note: Shared helpers of the telephony calls stack, named for it and placed beside the call history daemons in the reference image; BifrOSt has no cellular calls for them to serve.

entries.name: CallsXPC
entries.note: Service interface of the telephony calls stack, named for it and placed beside the calls service daemon in the reference image; BifrOSt has no cellular calls for it to carry.

entries.name: CallstackAnalysis

entries.ready_note: Call-stack tree built from diagnostic samples (sdk/src/call_stack_tree.rs) is tested.

entries.name: CameraColorProcessing
entries.note: The colour step of camera frames (NV12 to RGBA with a selectable colour matrix, media/convert.rs); no white balance or sensor colour tuning is built. Built 2026-10-17: gray-world white balance (media/convert.rs white_balance, tests in convert::tests), applied to saved photos in shell/camera save_capture. Still open: sensor colour tuning, and the live preview is not balanced. Built 2026-10-17: the live preview is white-balanced with gains smoothed across frames (convert::Smoothed, test the_preview_gains_move_gradually_toward_the_scene), and photos are balanced (save_capture). Still open: sensor colour tuning, which needs per-sensor data no BifrOSt driver reads.

entries.ready_note: Markdown line classes for notes (shell/md.rs) are tested; assistant answers are not rendered as Markdown.
